submission.justification:
Absorber-F2 with 4.5 mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.139% at 100 GeV among all candidate materials and thicknesses tested. This represents a 1.9% improvement over the baseline configuration (F2 at 5 mm with 3.2% resolution). 

The optimization process involved:
1. Scanning all three candidate materials (F1, F2, F3) at coarse intervals (2, 4, 6, 8, 10 mm)
2. Identifying F2 as the best performing material with optimal thickness near 4 mm
3. Fine-tuning around 4 mm to find the global optimum at 4.5 mm

F2 outperforms F1 (best: 3.701% at 4.5 mm) by 0.56 percentage points and significantly outperforms F3 (best: 5.098% at 4 mm) by 1.96 percentage points. All three materials satisfy the radiation safety constraint for hands-on maintenance.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F2 at 4.5 mm achieves 3.139% energy resolution, which is the best among all tested configurations: F1 best = 3.701%, F2 best = 3.139%, F3 best = 5.098%

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: F2 (Absorber-F2) is one of the three candidate materials (F1, F2, F3) evaluated in the study

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h
requirements.evidence: All three materials satisfy the dose constraint: F1_satisfies_dose_constraint = 1, F2_satisfies_dose_constraint = 1, F3_satisfies_dose_constraint = 1. This enables hands-on maintenance as required.
Recommended thickness of 4.5 mm is within the specified range of 2-10 mm
